options.description: Slice #36. Opt-in per-run toggles that shape how the kernel treats partially-specified programs. Absent is default (backward-compatible with all pre-#36 fixtures).

strict_framing.description: When true, effect / probability queries whose referenced predicates still have A0 framing gaps flip to needs_investigation before numeric evaluation. The F1 DEFINE_VARIABLE channel still fires with the same skeletons so the fill-back loop is unchanged — only the numeric path is gated.

cluster.description: Name of a data column carrying a cluster / block id (families, repeated measures, schools). Consumed only by the numeric estimation path (themis.estimate): every estimator's bootstrap CI then resamples whole clusters (pairs cluster bootstrap) instead of i.i.d. rows — the correct variance under within-cluster dependence. The column is a variance concern, not a causal-model node: it never appears as a variable/edge in the DAG and is excluded from the data hash. Identification (themis.run) ignores it.

ate_estimator.description: Selects the estimator for the backdoor-identified ATE on the numeric path (themis.estimate). 'gformula' (default) is the outcome-regression plug-in; 'ipw' is inverse-probability weighting on the propensity; 'aipw' is the doubly-robust augmented estimator (consistent if EITHER the outcome OR the propensity model is correct). Only the backdoor branch honours this — front-door / IV / mediation keep their own estimators. Identification (themis.run) ignores it.

longitudinal.description: Phase 7.L. Opt-in spec routing themis.estimate to the longitudinal parametric g-formula (g-computation) for a TIME-VARYING treatment strategy (Hernán & Robins, What If, ch.21). Declares the time ordering of treatments and covariates that the cross-sectional query AST cannot express. When present, the estimator fits L_k|history transition models + the outcome model, Monte-Carlo simulates always-treat vs never-treat, and attaches a longitudinal_gformula block to the first effect-query result.

treatments.description: Ordered (A_0..A_K) binary treatment column names, earliest first.

confounders_by_time.description: Parallel to treatments. Entry k lists covariates L_k measured after A_{k-1} and before A_k; index 0 is the baseline covariates L_0. Inner arrays may be empty.

confidence.description: Composite confidence score for the whole input item; not a statistical interval.

evidence.description: Phase 4 / A2: free-text evidence quote(s) supporting this annotation. String for a single source paragraph; list of strings when merged across multiple narrative extractions. Reasoning rules do not read this — it is provenance metadata for downstream rendering / audit only.

annotations.description: Slice A2: provenance / confidence metadata for this edge, e.g. {"source": "llm_proposal"} for a hypothesis edge, {"source": "PubMed:..."} for an evidence-backed edge. Reasoning rules do not read this.

coefficient.description: Linear-SCM path coefficient α on this edge (child = ... + α·from + ...). Optional metadata consumed ONLY by the scm_counterfactual query (Pearl Primer §4.2 abduction-action-prediction); qualitative DAG reasoning never reads it. A fully-specified linear SCM carries a coefficient on every edge along the path to the target.

populationName.description: Phase 9 §T9.1: a population identifier. Used to label probability statements with the source population they came from, and to label queries with the target population whose effect is wanted. Must be a valid identifier (snake_case recommended).

selectionNodeStatement.description: Phase 9 §T9.1. A selection node in a Bareinboim-Pearl selection diagram. Declares that the variable named in ``affects`` has a different distribution between the source and target populations — the canonical reason transport identification needs adjustment. Reasoning rules read it; verifier audits S-admissibility against it.

id.description: Stable identifier for this S node (e.g. ``S_age``). Used in derivation steps so the user can trace which S node a transport step references.

affects.description: The atom whose distribution differs across populations. Conceptually there is an arrow S → affects in the selection diagram; this field declares that arrow's head.

annotations.description: Provenance / evidence for the claim that distributions differ (e.g. {"source": "narrative_proposal", "evidence": "源人群均值 42 岁; 目标 28 岁"}). Reasoning does not read this.

bidirectedStatement.description: Phase 2.latent S1. An undirected 'bidirected' edge between two observed atoms, semantically declaring the existence of at least one unobserved common cause (semi-Markov representation). The runtime dispatches bidirected edges through the ADMG-aware identification path (m-separation + c-component / Tian-Shpitser ID), with IV / Balke-Pearl / Manski bounds as the escape layer when non-parametric point identification fails. See PHASE_2_LATENT_CHARTER.md.

annotations.description: Provenance / confidence metadata for the bidirected edge. Not consumed by reasoning rules in S1.

target.description: Target atom with the specific value this conditional refers to, e.g. {atom: cancer(X), value: true}.

given.description: Model conditioning set for the target, each entry a groundedAtom at a specific value. When provenance is 'structural' (default) this must be a subset of the target's structural parent set (∪ ancestors ∪ bidirected siblings, per iter 168). When provenance is 'observational' (relaxed mode, iter 2026-05-14) given can contain any atoms — useful when the supplied value is an empirical/joint-derived observational conditional (e.g. P(effort | accepted, talent) where accepted is a descendant of effort in the DAG, as in CLadder collider-shape questions).

value.description: Model-world conditional probability value, not an empirical sample frequency.

provenance.description: Source category for this probability entry. 'structural' (default) = user-stated CPT, strict parent-subset validation. 'observational' = empirical conditional that may condition on non-parents (CLadder Q6772 Berkson-style); validation relaxed, consumed only by direct lookup queries. 'llm_prior' (Fix 3+4, v0.1.5) = LLM-proposed prior from common knowledge when InsufficientTheta on the first run; strict parent-subset validation applies AND annotations.source is REQUIRED non-empty (a one-sentence reason that surfaces in extensions.llm_proposed_review for end-user audit before trusting the answer). Bounded fallback only — LLM must not proactively supply llm_prior on the first turn; charter FIX_3_4_CHARTER_llm_mediated_transport.md §1.4.

population.description: Phase 9 §T9.1: optional source-population label. Probability statements without this field are treated as universal across populations (back-compat).

given.description: Condition set for the structural association query.

target.description: Target atom with the specific value whose probability under intervention is being queried, e.g. {atom: cancer(alice), value: true}.

extra_interventions.description: Joint interventions: when present and non-empty, the query asks for the JOINT effect of intervening on the primary `intervention` AND every entry here simultaneously — do(A=a, B=b, ...). The primary intervention plus these extras form the joint treatment vector. Identification uses the generalized (treatment-set) back-door criterion; estimation uses the joint g-formula including the treatment×treatment interaction. Omitting the field (or supplying an empty array) preserves single-treatment total-effect semantics byte-for-byte. v1 scope: binary treatments, no directed edge between treatments, not combined with mediator / target_population.

given.description: Observed condition set applied together with the intervention, each at a specific value.

mediator.description: Phase 6.mediation: when present, the query asks for a mediation decomposition (NDE/NIE/CDE) through this mediator atom rather than a plain total effect. Omitting the field preserves total-effect semantics.

target_population.description: Phase 9 §T9.1: when present, the effect is wanted in this target population, not in the population the data was collected from. Triggers transport identification — requires at least one selectionNodeStatement to be meaningful.

assumptions.description: Iter 131: first-class assumption block parallel to CounterfactualQuery.assumptions. Optional. Currently carries optional `monotonicity` for the iter 119 Manski-Tamer bounds path; promoted from the iter 119 program.extensions['monotonicity'] side-channel hack to a query-level field. Scheduler still falls back to extensions when this is absent for backwards compat.

monotonicity.description: Direction of monotone treatment response (Manski 1997). When set, EffectQuery's bounds layer tightens one side of Manski natural to the observed marginal. Same semantic as CounterfactualQuery.assumptions.monotonicity.

given.description: Observed condition set for the interventional quantity to be identified.

target_population.description: Phase 9 §T9.1: when present, asks whether the interventional quantity is identifiable in this target population (transport identification). Requires at least one selectionNodeStatement.

target.description: Target atom with the specific value whose conditional probability is being queried.

observed.description: Observed factual world assignment, e.g. chose_major=false.

counterfactual_target.description: Counterfactual target event whose probability is being queried.

causationQuery.description: Probabilities of causation (Tian & Pearl 2000): PN (necessity), PS (sufficiency), PNS. cause (X) and effect (Y) are binary atoms. The observational joint P(X,Y) is recovered from theta; the two interventional risks P(Y=1|do(X=1/0)) are derived via effect identification, OR supplied directly via experimental_risk_treated/control for the confounded-but-experimentally-measured case (Tian-Pearl's drug example).

cause.description: Binary cause atom X. PN/PS/PNS are defined for binary X.

effect.description: Binary effect atom Y. PN/PS/PNS are defined for binary Y.

monotonic.description: When true, asserts Y is monotonic in X (X never prevents Y), which point-identifies all three quantities (Tian-Pearl Thm 3). When false/absent, only assumption-free bounds are returned.

experimental_risk_treated.description: Optional directly-supplied P(Y=1 | do(X=1)) from a randomized experiment. Use when the effect of X on Y is NOT identifiable from observational data alone (confounded) but an RCT measured the interventional risk separately (Tian-Pearl drug example). When absent, the risk is derived from theta via effect identification.

experimental_risk_control.description: Optional directly-supplied P(Y=1 | do(X=0)). Counterpart to experimental_risk_treated; supply both or neither.

scmCounterfactualQuery.description: Deterministic counterfactual point on a fully-specified linear SCM (Pearl Primer §4.2: abduction-action-prediction). Each cause edge on the path to the target must carry a `coefficient`; the unit's factual values come from observation statements (Pearl's evidence E=e). Returns the exact value `target` would have taken under `intervention` for that unit — a POINT, not a Balke-Pearl bound.

intervention.description: do(X=x): the variable to fix and the value to fix it at.

target.description: The variable whose counterfactual value is computed.

variableDeclaration.description: Advisory per-predicate framing metadata (slice A0). Declaring a variable opts it into framing_notes: any unset field becomes a gap reported on queries that reference this predicate. Omitting a declaration silences framing for that predicate; nothing here gates reasoning.

domain.description: Enumerated value domain, e.g. [true, false] or ["low","mid","high"]. Used only for framing; the runtime still reads actual domains from observed values.

time_window.description: Natural-language time window the variable refers to, e.g. "12w" or "single exam".

measurement.description: How the variable is measured, e.g. "waist circumference cm" or "self-reported daily minutes".

threshold.description: Cutoff that turns a continuous measurement into this predicate's value, e.g. ">=3cm".

observability.description: Whether the variable is observable / self-reported / latent in this setting.

direction.description: Slice #41. Effect polarity the predicate commits to: e.g. "up" (the predicate fires when the underlying quantity increases), "down", "mixed". Surfaces questions where '影响 X' is ambiguous between raise / lower / fluctuate.

baseline.description: Slice #41. The reference level a change is measured from, e.g. "pre-intervention clinic BP", "school-reported mid-term score". Surfaces questions like '提高数学成绩' where improvement relative to what baseline is not stated.

state_vs_event.description: Slice #41. Whether the predicate describes a habitual / persistent state or a discrete event: "state" vs "event". Surfaces ambiguity between e.g. '跟同事闹矛盾' as a one-off episode versus an ongoing relational state.
